accelerators.name: Movidius Myriad 2
accelerators.note: Vision processing unit; the whole payload computer draws a few watts.
accelerators.flown: ESA PhiSat-1 (2020), first neural inference in orbit

accelerators.name: Movidius Myriad X
accelerators.note: Flown inside the Ubotica CogniSAT / Unibap iX10 payload computers.

accelerators.name: Versal AI Core XQR VC1902
accelerators.note: Radiation-tolerant adaptive SoC; AI engines plus programmable logic.

accelerators.name: Jetson Orin NX 16 GB
accelerators.note: COTS module; the usual choice for on-board inference on a 6U-12U bus.

accelerators.name: Jetson AGX Orin 64 GB
accelerators.note: Configurable 15-60 W; quoted at its maximum sustained mode.
accelerators.flown: COTS; space-qualified carriers offered by several vendors

accelerators.name: Jetson AGX Thor
accelerators.note: Blackwell-generation edge module; the top of the low-power class.

accelerators.name: Cloud AI 100 Standard
accelerators.note: Passively cooled inference card; needs a host, unlike the SoCs above.

accelerators.name: L4
accelerators.note: Single-slot inference GPU; the lowest-power part in the server line.

accelerators.name: A100 PCIe 80 GB
accelerators.note: Ampere training GPU, PCIe form factor.

accelerators.name: H100 PCIe 80 GB
accelerators.note: The power-capped H100; the variant an orbital payload would choose.

accelerators.name: H100 SXM5 80 GB
accelerators.note: Full-power H100. Doubling board power buys 31 % more throughput.
accelerators.flown: Starcloud-1 (Nov 2025), first datacenter GPU in orbit

accelerators.name: B200 SXM
accelerators.note: Blackwell; the current upper end of single-package datacenter power.
